summary: Robeson County, NC, tower built by the CCC in 1935. Offered at a government surplus auction in 2014; no current status found in sources.

facts.design: 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with a 2-room ground cabin
facts.status_note: The last dated event in the sources is a January 2014 surplus auction; no source describes the tower's condition or location since.
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with a 2-room ground cabin; cost $1,714.68 through the Emergency Conservation Works program.
Session law directed the Division of Forest Resources to transfer the tower and about 0.9 acre by gift to the East Howellsville Volunteer Fire Department.
Tower and land offered at government surplus auction; closing January 28, 2014; winning bid with fees $8,922.50. Buyer not named in the source.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts listing pairs tower with NC Division of Forest Resources and East Howellsville Volunteer Fire Department
evidence.quote: Robeson County - North Carolina Division of Forest Resources > East Howellsville Volunteer Fire Department

evidence.supports: CCC built a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with ground cabin in February 1935
evidence.quote: February 1935: The Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower with a 2-room ground cabin for the cost of $1,714.68.

evidence.supports: funding through Emergency Conservation Works program
evidence.quote: The funding was through the Emergency Conservation Works program.

evidence.supports: figures sourced to the 6th Biennial report 1934-36
evidence.quote: (Department of Conservation and Development - 6th Biennial report 1934-36)

evidence.supports: 1993 session law as the source of the transfer text
evidence.quote: Session laws and resolutions passed by the General Assembly [1993]

evidence.supports: 1993 act directs transfer by gift to the fire department; location eight miles east of Lumberton
evidence.quote: shall transfer in fee simple by gift the East Robeson Fire Tower and approximately .91827 acres of land on which the tower is located approximately eight miles east of Lumberton on Highway 41 in East Howellsville Township, Robeson County

evidence.supports: land is the property in the March 7, 1935 deed to the fire department
evidence.quote: this being the property described in the deed dated March 7, 1935, and recorded in Deed Book 8-N, page 219, Robeson County registry to the East Howellsville Volunteer Fire Department, Inc.

evidence.supports: January 2014 surplus auction of tower and land
evidence.quote: January 2014: Government auction for surplus property: the 99'9" steel tower and the nine-tenths of an acre the tower is located are being sold at auction.
The winning bid total, plus fees, was $8,922.50.

notes_for_editor: Every dated fact comes from one page, the Forest Lookouts North Carolina list, which quotes a 1935 CCC entry, a 1993 session law and a 2014 auction notice. The session law and auction notice were not fetched at source. Two web searches, one aimed at the 2014 auction, found no independent confirmation of the sale or buyer. No source read explains how the 1993 transfer and the 2014 sale relate; the story gives them in order. The brief's unknown status is kept; no corrections to the brief.
